title: The day of the LORD: Jerusalem taken, the Mount of Olives split, living waters, the nations keep Booths (Zech 14)
speaker: The LORD (through the prophet)
description: The nations gather against Jerusalem and half the city goes into exile; the LORD fights for it, his feet stand on the Mount of Olives, which splits east to west; the people flee as from the earthquake in Uzziah's days; living waters flow east and west; the LORD becomes king over all the earth; the nations' survivors go up yearly to keep the Feast of Booths; "Holy to the LORD" on the horses' bells.

interpretations.label: A literal future return of the Messiah to the Mount of Olives and a millennial reign
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the siege of AD 70 lacks the deliverance described; the feet on the Mount of Olives are literal (cf. Acts 1:11–12; Rev 19:14); the nations keep Tabernacles in the millennium.

referents.symbol: The LORD whose feet stand on the Mount of Olives

interpretations.label: Figurative picture of the consummation of God's kingdom
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the living water is, as in Joel 3:18 and Ezek 47, a figure of salvation flowing from the centre of God's kingdom; the exaltation of Jerusalem is figurative like that of the temple mountain (Isa 2:2).

interpretations.label: Apocalyptic vision of a Greek-period writer; the Uzziah earthquake comparison a gloss
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the original described the stopping of a spring; a glossator added the comparison with the flight before the earthquake in Uzziah's days — the earthquake of Amos 1:1, which Josephus links with Uzziah's intrusion into the temple.
